title: When the Crown Turns
premise: Astrid Voss has spent her life as a bone-carver in the border town of Thornfell, carving names for the dead and hearing their last whispers—until she finds tonight's date inscribed in a century-old prophecy book that predicts her death at the moon's thirteenth turn. The prophecy speaks of a door out of Vessany, a country erased from maps forty years ago, and of a crown that 'turns' whoever wears it into someone else entirely. Hunted by the Regency's inquisitors who want the prophecy destroyed, Astrid follows the dead through smuggler roads into the drowned ruins of old Vessany, discovering she is the unrecognized heir of its deposed royal line—and that the 'door' is her own choice to claim or refuse the turning crown. In the end, Astrid breaks the crown rather than wear it, opening the door not to escape but to let Vessany's exiled dead finally cross over and rest, while she remains, visible at last, as the country's living memory.
about_author: Orsen Iversen is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping disputed borders before turning to fiction about places that refuse to stay on maps. They live in a coastal town with too many lighthouses and write at night, when the dead are said to be most talkative.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Hers
chapters.summary: Astrid carves a memorial bone for a drowned ferryman and hears him whisper a warning she doesn't understand. That night, browsing the smuggler-bookstall, she finds a prophecy book from a century ago with tonight's date inked beside a drawing of her own hands. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: unease—the first crack in her carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: What the Ferryman Knew
chapters.summary: Astrid interrogates the ferryman's ghost along the river road; he speaks of a door, a thirteenth moon, and a name he refuses to say aloud. An inquisitor arrives in Thornfell asking after an old book. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve—she realizes the book must be hidden or destroyed, and neither is safe.

chapters.title: Ink and Interrogation
chapters.summary: The inquisitor, Serel Dane, interviews Astrid under pretense of customs inspection; she lies well but notices he wears a signet of Vessany—the vanished country. Her grandmother's locked chest hums when she passes. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into curiosity about her own family's buried past.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Chest
chapters.summary: Astrid opens the chest with a key carved from her mother's finger-bone: inside, royal regalia fragments, a map of Vessany, and letters naming her bloodline. The dead in the walls begin whispering her true name. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: vertigo—identity upended; the belonging she craved arrives as a death sentence.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Astrid counts the lunar calendar: twelve turns remain before the prophecy's date. She tests the prophecy by avoiding a predicted small mishap—it happens anyway, differently. POV: Astrid, with a brief interlude from Serel reporting to his Regency masters. Emotional beat: claustrophobia of fate; free will feels like an illusion with teeth.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Bargain
chapters.summary: Astrid seeks out Yeva Kroll, the blind smuggler who knows the old Vessany roads, trading three carved bones for passage. Yeva warns: the mountains remember the country they ate. POV: Yeva. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; two women who survive by being unmemorable recognize each other.

chapters.title: Roads That No Longer Exist
chapters.summary: Crossing into the high passes, the party walks roads only the dead can see clearly; ghosts of Vessani soldiers march alongside, saluting Astrid without knowing why. Serel's hunters close behind. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: eerie wonder tinged with grief—a whole nation walking beside her, unseen.

chapters.title: The Village Under the Snow
chapters.summary: They shelter in a valley village whose inhabitants speak dead Vessani dialect and venerate a 'sleeping queen.' Astrid is recognized by a birthmark; the elders kneel. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: terror of being seen—her lifelong wish for belonging granted in the most dangerous form possible.

chapters.title: Serel's Doubt
chapters.summary: Serel captures one of Yeva's runners and learns the Regency plans to raze the valley villages to erase Vessany's last traces. His faith in his orders cracks. POV: Serel. Emotional beat: disillusionment—the hunter realizing he serves the eraser, not the law.

chapters.title: The Drowned Capital
chapters.summary: They reach Old Vessany, half-sunk beneath a reservoir built by the Regency; Astrid walks flooded streets breathing through carved bone charms, guided by thousands of patient dead. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: awe and sorrow—the beautiful corpse of a country, waiting for someone to mourn it properly.

chapters.title: The Turning Crown
chapters.summary: In the sunken palace, Astrid finds the crown of Vessany; touching it, she experiences a vision of every heir who wore it, each one overwritten until nothing of themselves remained. The prophecy's meaning clarifies: the crown turns, and it never gives back. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: horror—inheritance revealed as annihilation.

chapters.title: Yeva's Price
chapters.summary: Yeva reveals she was once Vessani court cartographer, blinded for refusing to surrender the maps; she has guided Astrid all along to finish her own unfinished duty. Their bargain sours and mends. POV: Yeva. Emotional beat: guilt confessed, trust reforged—belonging means being known, flaws included.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Waterline
chapters.summary: Regency troops seal the reservoir's edge; Serel, ordered to flood the ruins again with everyone inside, stalls and is arrested for treason. Astrid watches from the water, unable to intervene. POV: Serel. Emotional beat: sacrifice—the enemy becoming an ally at personal ruin.

chapters.title: The Dead Vote
chapters.summary: The ghosts of Vessany gather in the palace hall and, for the first time in forty years, argue: some want Astrid crowned so the nation lives again; others beg her to break the crown and let them die. POV: Astrid amid the assembly. Emotional beat: crushing weight of inheritance—an entire people's hope and grief resting on her shoulders.

chapters.title: Twelfth Turn
chapters.summary: One turn remains. Astrid attempts to leave through the prophesied door and finds it sealed—it opens only for one who either fully claims or fully renounces the crown. There is no third path, no invisibility. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: despair—the middle way she built her life around does not exist here.

chapters.title: What Astrid Voss Is Made Of
chapters.summary: Alone among the dead, Astrid carves her own memorial bone, listing honestly who she is—not a queen, not a ghost, but a maker of names. The act clarifies her: identity is what you carve, not what you inherit. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: quiet self-recognition; the theme crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Crown
chapters.summary: On the thirteenth turn's eve, Astrid takes the crown to the palace forge and shatters it with her carving hammer, renouncing the throne. The dead do not rage—they exhale, forty years of held breath released. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: catharsis—refusing the crown is not betrayal but mercy.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Vessany
chapters.summary: With the crown broken, the prophesied door opens in the reservoir wall: not an escape route, but a crossing for the dead. The ghosts of Vessany file through toward rest, each pausing to touch Astrid's hands in thanks. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: bittersweet release—she saves a country by letting it go.

chapters.title: Serel's Choice
chapters.summary: Freed by sympathetic soldiers as the flooding begins, Serel holds the Regency line long enough for Astrid and Yeva to escape the ruins, then surrenders himself to testify about the planned atrocities. POV: Serel. Emotional beat: redemption purchased with consequence—he chooses accountability over safety.

chapters.title: The Country That Remembers
chapters.summary: Astrid and Yeva return to the valley villages, where the elders learn their queen chose them over the crown. Astrid begins carving a new kind of monument: bones bearing every recovered Vessani name, a country made of memory instead of territory. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: purpose found—belonging rebuilt on chosen ground.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon
chapters.summary: The prophecy's date arrives; Astrid stands unafraid as the moon completes its turn, and nothing kills her—the prophecy fulfilled itself in the breaking, the door, the crossing. Serel's testimony reaches the capital; the Regency wobbles. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: triumph without victory-lust—survival as quiet revolution.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: Months later, Astrid keeps her shop in Thornfell, openly Vessani, teaching village children to carve names for their dead. A traveler asks if she regrets refusing a kingdom; she answers that she got something rarer—a self. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: peace and belonging earned, the story's themes resolved in a single warm scene.
